outputs.L1: In this note, we develop tools and techniques for the analysis of anisotropic thermoelasticity in two spatial dimensions. Using a diagonalisation technique, we establish properties of the characteristic roots of the system’s full symbol and thereby prove \(L^p\)–\(L^q\) decay rates for its solutions.
outputs.L2: This note establishes methods for analyzing two-dimensional anisotropic thermoelastic systems. By diagonalizing the system’s full symbol, we investigate its characteristic roots and derive \(L^p\!-\!L^q\) decay estimates for the corresponding solutions.
outputs.L3: This note develops analytical tools and techniques for studying anisotropic thermo-elasticity in two spatial dimensions. Its central approach is a diagonalisation procedure applied to the full symbol of the coupled thermo-elastic system. This procedure provides a detailed understanding of the system’s characteristic roots, including their asymptotic behavior and structural properties. The resulting information about the characteristic roots is then used to derive \(L^p\)–\(L^q\) decay estimates for solutions, thereby describing their long-time behavior in appropriate function spaces.
outputs.L4:
This work investigates the long-time behavior of solutions to the two-dimensional anisotropic thermoelastic system. The coupling between elastic displacement and temperature produces a mixed hyperbolic–parabolic structure whose qualitative properties depend strongly on the direction of propagation. After applying the spatial Fourier transform, the system is reduced to a parameter-dependent first-order system. Its full symbol is then analyzed through a systematic diagonalization procedure.

Particular attention is given to the characteristic roots of the symbol. Their asymptotic behavior is studied in the low- and high-frequency regimes, as well as near directions in which the elastic modes may degenerate or interact weakly with the thermal component. The resulting eigenvalue expansions reveal the different mechanisms governing wave propagation, thermal diffusion, and dissipation. They also identify which modes are effectively damped and which retain predominantly oscillatory behavior.

Using suitable frequency decompositions and estimates for the associated Fourier multipliers, we derive \(L^p\)–\(L^q\) decay bounds for the solution and its relevant derivatives. These estimates quantify how the decay depends on time, spatial dimension, anisotropy, and the regularity and integrability of the initial data. The analysis distinguishes contributions from low frequencies, which determine the principal large-time asymptotics, from high frequencies, where additional regularity may be required.

Overall, the results provide a detailed description of the interaction between anisotropic elastic waves and heat conduction in two dimensions. The diagonalization of the full symbol not only clarifies the spectral structure of the system but also leads to precise decay rates, thereby giving a rigorous account of the solutions’ long-time behavior.

counterfactuals.output: We study large-time decay for solutions to the Cauchy problem for anisotropic thermo-elastic systems in two spatial dimensions. After a microlocal diagonalization of the Fourier-transformed system, the asymptotic behavior is related to the geometry of the elastic Fresnel curves and to the order of vanishing of the thermo-elastic coupling functions along hyperbolic directions. Under suitable non-degeneracy assumptions, we derive sharp \(L^{p}\!-\!L^{q}\) estimates for the solution and its energy. The decay rates depend on the curvature and contact order of the characteristic curves, and may differ substantially from those in the isotropic case. Special attention is given to directions in which elastic waves decouple from the thermal component, where weak damping leads to slower decay. The results are illustrated for representative classes of anisotropic media.
